title: Keep asynchronous flows cancellation-aware and non-blocking
statement: Use async all the way for I/O, accept and propagate CancellationToken, use ConfigureAwait(false) in the reusable core library, and avoid .Result, .Wait(), fire-and-forget work, or cancellation converted into success.
rationale: Reviews and sensors can be long-running and highly concurrent. Blocking or dropped cancellation wastes worker capacity and can leave persisted review state inconsistent.

examples.good:
var result = await client.SendAsync(request, cancellationToken).ConfigureAwait(false);
await PersistAsync(result, cancellationToken).ConfigureAwait(false);

history.change: Initial .NET async-hygiene seed grounded in Quality Studio runners and sensors.
